Needs changes before merge. Safety review: one blocking defect. The branch also conflicts with main.

The new tests measure the stock at both open edges. They also check the distance from the cutter to a nearby part. The decision record explains the change to the sample test. No UI files, golden files, dependencies, or build scripts changed. I read each changed line of the sample test.

Requested before merge:

1. **[P1] Apply the new part check at posting time too.** `crates/app/src/operation/keep_law.rs:228` now includes Pocket3D and MultiAxisRough. But `crates/app/src/operation/kept_rejudge.rs:36` still excludes both kinds: `is_stock_kept_kind` is false and `depth_law_of` returns `None`. Thus `moved_part_problem` returns before it can check a part added after generation. When the program simulation cannot run, posting uses the old clean result and writes a cut through that part.

   I reproduced this with the new notch fixture. Set the square stock rotation to 90 degrees about Z. Create and generate a Pocket3D operation with the test's tool and parameters. Confirm that its status is `Ok`. Then import a second block at X [5, 10], Y [5, 10], Z [20, 30]. The operation stays `Ok`. A new generation detects the cut through the block. But the live post check returns `None`, and `posting::post_setup` succeeds and writes 335 lines of NC. Its only note says that the program simulation cannot judge rotated stock. I removed the output file after the test.

   Include both kinds in the live post check. Use the same kind rule as generation so the two checks cannot disagree. Add regression tests that generate a clean path, add or move a part into it, then require posting to refuse by name. Cover a rotated stock and MultiAxisRough.

Local results:

The trial merge with `upstream/main` at `e2f012e9` failed in `crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs:162`. Main expects the revised tool-clearance refusal; this PR expects a clean cut. I did not resolve this code conflict. I aborted the trial merge and ran all checks below on the PR head. Resolve this conflict at merge time and test the merged result. These results do not certify a merged tree.

I repeated two of the PR's mutations:

- Return the original footprint: the open-edge test failed with `the open edge keeps stock to Z 32.000 at (14.95, 10.80); the floor is Z 20`.
- Remove the neighbor keep-out: the neighbor test failed with 81 warnings instead of 0.

I restored both files byte for byte. All three open-side tests then passed. I also removed the temporary safety tests. The review worktree has no source changes.

The two extra safety tests failed as expected:

```text
the live post judge must catch this cut, got None
must refuse the cut through inner; posting returned Ok; wrote NC: true
```

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Fixed the P1 finding on live posting checks.

Generation and posting now use the same rule for kinds that must keep neighbouring parts clear. The rule includes Pocket3D and MultiAxisRough.

Tests:
- `pocket3d_post_refuses_a_part_added_after_clean_generation_on_rotated_stock`
- `multiaxis_rough_post_refuses_a_part_added_after_clean_generation_on_rotated_stock`

Both tests first generate a clean path and post it successfully. They then add a part into the cut on rotated stock. Posting refuses by operation and part name. It writes no NC file.

Mutation check: the old posting dispatch makes both tests fail. The restored fix makes both pass.

`cargo xtask gate quick --base upstream/main` passed: 2,197 tests passed, 24 ignored. App and motion clippy passed with `--all-targets -- -D warnings`.

New head: `6c458ec1f6072a2523bbe958bd4b065145ab4482`.

The known merge conflict remains for merge time, as the review directs. No merge was attempted.

Please re-review this head.

Code review clean. The earlier safety defect is fixed. The branch still conflicts with main.

Generation and posting now use the same rule to select operations that must keep other parts clear. The rule includes Pocket3D and MultiAxisRough. Both new tests first post a clean path. They then add a part into the cut on rotated stock. Posting refuses by operation and part name and writes no NC file.

This is a safety review. I read the geometry and posting changes. I also read each changed line of the sample assertion in `shared_face_bodies.rs`. The decision record explains why that test now expects a clean cut instead of a refusal. No golden files, UI files, dependencies, build scripts, or workflow files changed.

I repeated these safety mutations locally:

- Return the original footprint: the open-edge test failed. Stock stayed at Z 32.000 at (14.95, 10.80), above the Z 20 floor.
- Remove the neighbor keep-out: the neighbor test failed with 81 warnings instead of 0.
- Restore the old live-post dispatch: both new posting tests failed. The unsafe paths posted instead of being refused.

I restored both source files byte for byte. All five open-side tests then passed. The worktree has no source changes.

Requested code changes: none. The earlier P1 request is resolved on this head. Resolve the merge conflict at merge time and test the merged result before merge.

Nonblocking note: `generate.rs` was already over the file-size guide. This PR adds 11 lines there. The new geometry logic is in small modules.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.

Stopped at the merge conflict, as instructed for changes to the same logic.

The latest review requests no code changes. Its remaining request is to resolve the merge conflict and test the merged result.

Merging upstream/main at fe1a94c7 conflicts in crates/app/tests/shared_face_bodies.rs around line 164. The PR requires generation to succeed with status `ok` in `the_sample_as_imported_roughs_the_3d_pocket_beside_its_silhouette`. Main requires generation to fail with `nothing to cut: the open area is too narrow for the 6 mm tool and 0 mm stock to leave at every level`. The accompanying comments also state opposite cutter-clearance rules.

Both sides changed the same test logic. I did not choose either safety expectation. I aborted the merge. No changes were committed or pushed. The head remains 6c458ec1f6072a2523bbe958bd4b065145ab4482. The gate was not run because there is no resolved merged tree to test.
